title: Erdős #644: Covering Families of Sets
description: Let f(k,r) be the minimum size of a covering set for k-uniform families where every r sets share a common pair. Known: f(k,3)=2k, f(k,4)=⌊3k/2⌋, f(k,5)=⌊5k/4⌋, f(k,6)=k. Is f(k,7)=(3/4+o(1))k?

meta.author: Paul Erdős, Fon-Der-Flaass, Kostochka, Tuza

mathContext.subfield: Covering numbers of structured set families
mathContext.significance: Determines the precise covering efficiency of k-uniform set families under r-wise pair coherence. The known exact values f(k,3)=2k through f(k,6)=k reveal a decreasing coefficient sequence c₃=2, c₄=3/2, c₅=5/4, c₆=1. The open questions ask whether c₇=3/4 (crossing below the natural barrier c=1) and whether the linear-in-k behavior persists for all r.

originalContributions: PairIntersects / HasRWisePairProperty: r-wise pair coherence condition
Known values axioms: f(k,3)=2k, f(k,4)=⌊3k/2⌋, f(k,5)=⌊5k/4⌋, f(k,6)=k
Monotonicity: f non-increasing in r, non-decreasing in k

overview.historicalContext:
Erdős, Fon-Der-Flaass, Kostochka, and Tuza introduced this problem in 1992, studying the covering function f(k,r) for k-uniform set families with the r-wise pair intersection property. They determined exact values for r = 3, 4, 5, 6, revealing a striking pattern of decreasing coefficients: c₃ = 2, c₄ = 3/2, c₅ = 5/4, c₆ = 1.

The r-wise pair property is a Helly-type condition: it requires that any r sets in the family are linked by a common pair intersecting all of them. As r increases, the condition becomes stronger, forcing more structure on the family and enabling smaller covering sets. The sequence of exact values suggests a regular pattern, but no general formula has been established.

The problem connects to several important themes in combinatorics: the sunflower lemma (Erdős-Rado 1960), Helly-type theorems, hypergraph transversal theory, and the recently improved sunflower bounds (Alweiss-Lovett-Wu-Zhang 2020). The open questions about f(k,7) and general asymptotics probe the fundamental limits of covering efficiency under structural constraints.
overview.problemStatement: Let f(k,r) be minimal such that if A₁, A₂, ... is a family of k-sets where every r sets share a common pair {x,y} intersecting all of them, then some set of size f(k,r) intersects all Aᵢ. Q1: Is f(k,7) = (3/4 + o(1))k? Q2: For all r ≥ 3, does f(k,r) = (c_r + o(1))k for some constant c_r?
overview.text: Let f(k,r) be the minimum size of a covering set for k-uniform families where every r sets share a common pair. Known: f(k,3)=2k, f(k,4)=⌊3k/2⌋, f(k,5)=⌊5k/4⌋, f(k,6)=k. Is f(k,7)=(3/4+o(1))k?
overview.proofStrategy: The formalization defines the combinatorial primitives (k-families, pair intersection, r-wise pair property, covering sets), states the central function f(k,r), axiomatizes the four known exact values from EFKT92, formalizes the coefficient pattern and monotonicity properties, establishes the sunflower connection, and states the two open questions about f(k,7) and general asymptotics.
keyInsights: Coefficients decrease: c₃=2, c₄=3/2, c₅=5/4, c₆=1, conjectured c₇=3/4
c₆=1 is a natural barrier: covering set = individual set size
f(k,r) is non-increasing in r (stronger coherence helps) and non-decreasing in k
The r-wise pair property is a Helly-type condition weaker than sunflower structure
Recent sunflower lemma improvements (ALWZ 2020) may inform approaches to this problem

sections.title: Basic Definitions
sections.summary: Defines `KFamily` (k-uniform set family), `PairIntersects` (pair shares element with set), `HasRWisePairProperty` (every r sets linked by common pair), and `IsCoveringSet` (set intersects all family members).
sections.mathContext: Defines `KFamily` (k-uniform set family), `PairIntersects` (pair shares element with set), `HasRWisePairProperty` (every r sets linked by common pair), and `IsCoveringSet` (set intersects all family members).

sections.title: The Function f(k,r)
sections.summary: Defines the central covering function f(k,r): the minimum covering set size for k-uniform families with the r-wise pair property.
sections.mathContext: $f(k,r) = \max\{\tau(\mathcal{F}) : \mathcal{F} \text{ is } k\text{-uniform with the } r\text{-wise pair property}\}$, where $\tau$ is the minimum transversal size. Measures worst-case covering cost under structural coherence.

sections.title: Known Values (EFKT92)
sections.summary: Axiomatizes the four known exact values: f(k,3)=2k, f(k,4)=⌊3k/2⌋, f(k,5)=⌊5k/4⌋, f(k,6)=k, each requiring matching upper and lower bounds.
sections.mathContext: $f(k,3) = 2k$, $f(k,4) = \lfloor 3k/2 \rfloor$, $f(k,5) = \lfloor 5k/4 \rfloor$, $f(k,6) = k$ [EFKT92]. Each requires matching upper bound (algorithm) and lower bound (extremal construction).

sections.title: Pattern in Coefficients
sections.summary: Defines the coefficient sequence c₃=2, c₄=3/2, c₅=5/4, c₆=1 and formalizes the observed decreasing pattern.
sections.mathContext: Coefficients $c_r = f(k,r)/k$ as $k \to \infty$: $c_3 = 2$, $c_4 = 3/2$, $c_5 = 5/4$, $c_6 = 1$. The sequence is strictly decreasing. Note $c_6 = 1$: the covering set equals a single family member.

sections.title: Question 1: r = 7
sections.summary: States the open question: is f(k,7) = (3/4 + o(1))k? This would cross below the c=1 natural barrier.
sections.mathContext: OPEN: Is $f(k,7) = (3/4 + o(1))k$? If $c_7 = 3/4 < 1 = c_6$, then 7-wise coherence forces covering sets \emph{smaller} than a single family member — a qualitative phase transition.

sections.title: Question 2: General Asymptotics
sections.summary: States whether f(k,r) = (cᵣ + o(1))k for all r ≥ 3 with well-defined limiting coefficients.
sections.mathContext: OPEN: Does $\lim_{k \to \infty} f(k,r)/k = c_r$ exist for all $r \geq 3$? Known for $r \leq 6$. Would establish that $f$ is asymptotically linear in $k$ with a well-defined coefficient function $r \mapsto c_r$.

sections.title: Extremal Constructions
sections.summary: Describes lower-bound constructions showing the known values of f(k,r) are tight via partition-based families.
sections.mathContext: Lower bound constructions: partition-based $k$-uniform families achieving $\tau(\mathcal{F}) = c_r \cdot k$ while satisfying the $r$-wise pair property. These show the known values are tight.

sections.title: Monotonicity Properties
sections.summary: Formalizes f(k,r) non-increasing in r and non-decreasing in k, following from containment of pair properties.
sections.mathContext: $f(k, r+1) \leq f(k, r)$: stronger coherence (larger $r$) reduces covering cost. $f(k+1, r) \geq f(k, r)$: larger sets are harder to cover. Both follow from set containment of the pair property families.

sections.title: Sunflower Connection
sections.summary: Links the r-wise pair property to the Erdős-Rado sunflower lemma, with the pair property as a weaker structural guarantee.
sections.mathContext: An $r$-sunflower has $r$ sets sharing a common core. The $r$-wise pair property is weaker: every $r$ sets share \emph{some} common pair, not necessarily the same one. Improved sunflower bounds (ALWZ 2020: $(\log k)^{O(r)}$) may inform approaches.

sections.title: Hypergraph Formulation
sections.summary: Reformulates the covering problem in hypergraph language: f(k,r) is the transversal number of the pair-coherent k-uniform hypergraph.
sections.mathContext: In hypergraph language: $f(k,r) = \max \tau(\mathcal{H})$ over $k$-uniform hypergraphs $\mathcal{H}$ with the $r$-wise pair intersection property, where $\tau(\mathcal{H}) = \min |T|$ over transversals $T$ hitting every edge.

sections.title: Special Cases
sections.summary: Examines limiting behavior as k → ∞ and r → ∞ to understand the asymptotic landscape.
sections.mathContext: As $r \to \infty$: does $c_r \to 0$? If so, infinite coherence would make covering arbitrarily cheap relative to $k$. As $k \to \infty$ with $r$ fixed: the known values suggest $f(k,r) \sim c_r k$.

sections.title: Main Conjectures
sections.summary: Combines Question 1 and Question 2 into the main conjecture about the complete asymptotic structure of f(k,r).
sections.mathContext: Combined conjecture: $f(k,r) = (c_r + o(1))k$ for all $r \geq 3$, with $c_3 = 2 > c_4 = 3/2 > c_5 = 5/4 > c_6 = 1 > c_7 = 3/4 > \cdots$ strictly decreasing. Status: OPEN.

conclusion.summary: This formalization captures Erdős Problem #644 on covering families of sets with the r-wise pair property. The function f(k,r) measures covering efficiency under structural constraints, with exact values known for r = 3, 4, 5, 6 revealing a decreasing coefficient sequence. The two open questions — whether c₇ = 3/4 and whether cᵣ exists for all r — probe the fundamental asymptotics of this covering function.
conclusion.implications: Resolution of Question 1 would determine whether the coefficient sequence crosses below the natural barrier c = 1 Resolution of Question 2 would establish whether all r-wise pair families have linear-in-k covering numbers Understanding the limit of cᵣ as r → ∞ would reveal whether infinite coherence enables sublinear covering Connections to the sunflower lemma suggest that improved sunflower bounds may yield progress on f(k,r)
openQuestions: Does f(k,r) = (c_r + o(1))k for all r ≥ 3?
What is the limit of c_r as r → ∞?
Does f(k,r) eventually stabilize or continue decreasing?
